Team — quick tech summary from initial triage on the bridge:

Observations:
- Reserved quota counter for StablePay (res_bucket_id: RB-4782) shows sustained token allocation but our routing layer diverted ~37% of StablePay's requests to shared-fallback nodes between 08:38–08:52 due to a spike in sequence-length variance. The routing policy evaluated cost/latency and aged the reservation match incorrectly.
- Shared nodes experienced KV cache churn; heavy prefix reuse from a StablePay merchant batch amplified cache misses which increased tail latency and produced upstream 502s.
- Autoscaler did not trigger additional dedicated nodes because the policy threshold was on sustained avg CPU, but this event was high-throughput/short-duration and undercounted by the averaging window.
- No kernel OOMs; we saw higher retry rates from the worker layer (retries causing amplification).

Immediate mitigation completed (09:30–09:34):
- Reapplied strict routing policy: all StablePay production traffic is pinned to dedicated-burst pool (dedicated-burst-08) for the next 2 hours.
- Enabled rate-limiter on shared pool to cap noisy tenants (per-tenant throttle at 120 QPS).
- Increased autoscaler sensitivity for the reserved-pool metric to react to 1-min spikes; will monitor for oscillation.

Proposed short-term asks (need exec approval):
1) Approve temporary burst allocation (+4 GPUs) for 2 hours for StablePay (cost will be credited).
2) Approve a scope-1 postmortem and customer-facing summary to commit to an action plan.

Next steps:
- I'll push the full diagnostic bundle to the Drive link and attach the initial_obs_20270714.csv with span-level latencies.
- Ops will keep the bridge open and monitor 5-minute rolling tail latencies.

Attachments: reassign_policy.sh (policy script), initial_obs_20270714.csv (samples)
